utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. My apologies on behalf of the Tribunal for the confusion as to the courtroom. The Appeals Chamber had to have its hearing in Courtroom I. If somebody could take a look at Judge Baird's computer? Mine is working and we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis with Judge Howard Morrison sitting in the Appeals hearing of Lukic and Lukic. Before we continue with the cross-examination of this witness I have to ask Mr. Robinson the -- whether your submission yesterday or motion to strike out the cross-examination part of this witness in his previous transcript is something we have to rule upon? Was it a serious motion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we would prefer actually to have an adequate time for cross-examination and keep the entire transcript intact, but in the alternative we prefer to have more time for Dr. Karadzic's cross-examination, if you have reduced his time as a result of the inclusion of the Brdjanin cross. So our preference is to keep it all together but give him enough time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. That's consistent with our understanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, we weren't sure whether it was something on which we had to rule so we thought we would get from you exactly what your situation was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I don't think you have to explicitly rule on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Splendid. Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, your Excellency and good morning to everybody. I'm hearing the English now on channel 6. Can you hear the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you give it a try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope everything is working now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Because of protected witnesses, I'm not going to refer to you as your -- I sometimes refer to names but, Mr. Karabeg, is it true and correct that the Muslims, the officers, tried to dissuade you from armed action against the Serbs in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no barracks there, no officers or anything military, any military posts at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But a prominent officer, Muslim officer, was later the commander, the corps commander, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Mehmed Alagic. Mehmed Alagic retired and Mehmed Alagic dealt with different affairs. He didn't contact us in any way. Mehmed Alagic was in Travnik when he was expelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now take a look at 1D00013 next, please, on e-court. Before that he was an active JNA officer, was he not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you focus on the Serbian version that's been highlighted and this is an official note tailed [as interpreted] by the police, the Security Services Centre, and it says here that the subject is Mehmed Alagic. It gives his particulars and paragraph 2 says that he was going to be the commander of Territorial Defence in Sanski Most. That he was earmarked for that. Can you read this passage?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, read what it says there in that paragraph in the rectangle. It says here - does it not? - that the leaders of the SDA, Kurbegovic, Redzo; Karabeg, Mirzet; Sejfo Krantic; Halilovic, Nijaz conducted talks, tried to persuade him to join them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour, Mr. Karadzic is putting to this witness a statement of another witness which the Trial Chamber was dissuading him from doing previously. He can simply be putting any proposition he wishes to put to the witness without doing it in this manner, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I quite agree with you, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I have to disagree, with all due respect for the Trial Chamber and everybody else. This isn't a statement. It's an official note made by a secret police policeman. And it records what they learnt, the information gathered. It is not Alagic's statement as such.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not quite different from the statement. It is a result of its investigation or interview of this third person. You can just put your proposition to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. If I can just intervene on Dr. Karadzic's behalf. Yesterday, Dr. Karadzic asked this witness whether or not the Muslims were arming themselves and the answer that he got at first was, no, that's what you say, Dr. Karadzic, and then maybe some people were arming themselves. It was only after Dr. Karadzic showed him the book in which he was the executive editor, one of the editors, that the witness not only acknowledged that the Muslims were arming themselves but that he, himself, participated in the financing of the purchase of those arms which was in the book. Now if Dr. Karadzic is limited to simply putting propositions to a witness without confronting the witness with sources of that information, then he's not going to be as effective and the cross-examination will not be as correct as it can otherwise be, as productive for the Chamber as well. So I think he's entitled to do what he's doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, I do not disagree with you. What he first has to do is to put his proposition to the witness and then he can confront the witness with some other third party statement if possible -- if necessary. But don't start with reading out third party statements. That's what I'm telling him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. I think that's very correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I first asked about Alagic and the witness denied it. He said that Alagic did not engage anyone. He said that Alagic had nothing to do with them. Now this document shows that this particular witness, among those three or four men, tried to persuade Alagic to accept becoming the Territorial Defence commander. It was unsuccessful, but later on, he did take it up. So can you say -- can you tell us that this is what it says, that the 6th Krajina was strong and that you didn't need to do that.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was like this. You are putting something to me which comes from your organs, established erroneously and falsely by your organs. I didn't know Alagic at all before the war, nor was Alagic interesting in any way. And you are now putting this document to me from the security station in Prijedor where it says what it says. You could have said whatever you like, that I'm a murderer or that the person who sent the document can say that. Give me a document from a neutral side, from -- by our side. Don't send me documents from the Banja Luka Security Services Centre or what does it say here, Prijedor, it says which anybody could have wrote. That is your view of affairs, your thoughts. So you're doing that all the time. You're presenting your views that you were right because you killed 758 people in Sanski Most because allegedly they were guilty of something, of intending to do something, and so on and so forth. So read the header of this document, read what it says at the top. Can we zoom down, please so that we can see the top of the document? No persuasion, no discussion. It says here security centres Banja Luka, Prijedor department, and so on and so forth. So it's their organs, their authority, their men, their people, and who knows what they did. I don't. And now we should trust this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karabeg, all I'm saying is that General Alagic mentions you as one of four men who tried to recruit him and he said that he tried to dissuade you and to tell you that the 6th Krajina Brigade was a very strong brigade, it wasn't me that tried to persuade you of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You heard the witness's -- from the witness how or what he thinks about this document. That's what you received. Otherwise you need to call General Alagic if necessary. Don't argue with the witness. Just get on with the evidence you heard from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Mr. Alagic has died since but this is a state organ and this was recorded by that state organ, and I just wanted to put it to you because Karabeg accepts the fact that they had organisation and arms, he accepts that only when he's shown documents which state that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, can we take a look at 65 ter 4988 next, please? Is it true and correct, Mr. Karabeg, that you knew that the Serbs knew about all your actions, militarily organised actions and your arming? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. All I can do is laugh at that question of yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, can we have page 161, in Serbian, and it is 151 in English. It is the diary of the late Rasula. Can we turn to the previous page to see the date, which is 4 May 1992. Just briefly, in Serbian, the previous page to be displayed just to see the date. It was a session held on 4 May 1992. And it says KS, diacritic, and then 1992. Now, can we go back to the page we were on a moment ago? Next page, please. So we are interested actually in those two pages. It says the SDA, the areas of responsibility in the town. The first town command, the old fire station. The second town command, the primary school, elementary school. That's right. Thank you, that's fine. Second town command, the Vuk Karadzic elementary school. The third town command was Zdena Pobrijezje, probably a firm and then the commander, Sabic. Then we don't know who this Chief of Staff is, it just says Chief of Staff. Then the civilian protection commander, Ivan Filipovic and then added another name, Fajko, and then the chief of the public security station, Suad Sabic and so on and so forth. The chief of artillery, Colic, Mirsad. Did you know these people, did you know Nihad Kljucanin; Sabic, Suad; Mehmed Alagic; and the other names listed there, Mirsad Colic and so on? Did you know them?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd never heard of Mirsad Colic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Maybe his name is Calic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know Adem Zukic, for example?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was the chief of artillery in Sanski Most, the Muslim artillery, I mean?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radovan Karadzic. You're putting something to me which your closest associate wrote, and wrote in his diary at that. And now you're trying to display that as being evidence. When that diary was supposed to be adopted as an original document, you brought that into question at this Tribunal because of that word that was introduced here. So that's what I'm saying. Yes, the commander of the artillery was Radovan Karadzic. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Don't be angry at me. You can just --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not angry, I'm not angry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can say no.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May we turn to the next page, please? Let's look at the left-hand side, the number of armed units and their distribution, disposition. There are two detachments and two companies in Sana, then the 1st Company, 2nd Company, independent company, and then an independent platoon and so on. Then we have Modra, Zenkovici, Lukavice, Cirkici; they are all villages. Each village had a platoon or detachment. Kamengrad, et cetera. Was that the case or not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May we now take a look at the right-hand side? Now, Trnova, is that a Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about Caplje, and Tomina? Tomina is half-half, isn't it? There is Vrhpolje, has a detachment, Hrustovo, a detachment, Stara Rijeka, Majdan, Bartikovci, a detachment, Dzevar, a platoon. Are those all Muslim villages?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are. Small Muslim villages. Your Honours, I would like to ask you to ask him not to put these documents to me because they were written by Nedeljko Rasula, his closest ally and he wrote whatever he felt like writing down in his diary. As far as I know, they put into question their own material, the evidence just because of a word that was introduced in the Latin script.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, may I say this: Dr. Karadzic is defending himself and he is entitled to put these documents to you. It will be entirely a matter for you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: It will be entirely a matter for you if you accept it or you don't. You just say so. But he's entitled. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Moreover, if I can add this to what Judge Baird said is that this document was introduced by the Prosecution during their examination-in-chief of your evidence. So that is further reason for Mr. Karadzic to be entitled to put anything to you. But it is for you to say you don't know or do you know. It's for you to accept or not. Yes. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we turn to the next page, please, to see what was going on in Fajtovci.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is Fajtovci a Muslim village too?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I think it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says 20 automatic rifles, two PAPs, 40 to 50 pistols, 45 to 50 pistols, Ismet Alagic and Said Horozovic, commander and deputy commander. Sehovci, 20 automatic rifles, a total of 72 armed individuals, et cetera, et cetera. May we turn to the next page, please? Another page, please, next page. On the left bank in Sanski Most, who was -- who was on the left bank, Muslims, weren't they, mostly, the majority?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, roughly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, take a look at the composition of the independent company on the left bank. Said Besic, Ermin Sabic, Jasmin Jakupovic, Bekir Kovacevic and so on and so forth. All of them together made up the independent company. There are snipers there, mortars there, infantry, artillery, technical backup and so on and so forth, logistics. So, this is what the intelligence learnt by the Serb side about your military strength in town and around the town in the villages. Do you say that that is not correct or that you didn't know about it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true. Let me tell you something now. A man who is from Sanski Most, and who was at Manjaca, he was missing a leg, he didn't have a leg and he was caught as if he was climbing a 7-metre high tunnel and firing with a sniper. They captured him and said that that that's what he was doing. So that's the kinds of documents you're showing me. This is just not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that the Muslims in Sanski Most did not have any snipers and that they didn't use snipers to kill?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying. They did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to tender these pages into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Were they included in the part you tendered yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, they will be added.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Staying with that document, can we look at page 155 in Serbian and 141 in English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just for the record, can I know the Exhibit number of Mr. Rasula's diary?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's Exhibit P3329.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we zoom in to the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you read the Cyrillic script? You do, don't you, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when it's printed, yes, but I'm not so good with handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Colonel Basara here says that Redzo told him that it wasn't a good idea that he came with the army, with soldiers, and he says that he said that the MUP could be painlessly divided, and then Redzo wielded his influence and persuaded me not to bring in the army. And then he goes on to say the driver noticed that they were deploying snipers on the roofs and that this was organised by the Muslims. Do you see that? Do you see that Mr. Basara and you said of him that he was neutral, that he wanted to -- you said that he wanted to protect the Muslims from the Serb extremists. Now, was it his job to protect the Serbs from Muslim extremists as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, when I said this, I said that he'd led us astray, he duped us. We thought he was protecting us, but we knew straight away which side he sided with. We know who he was because he brought in the 6th Krajina Brigade from Pakrac. We know what he did to Sanski Most. I said that he duped us. We thought that he wanted to do what he said, but he did something quite different altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you can go on with this witness on these matters, but I think you can't simply complain about your shortage of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I want to put evidence to this witness, as you had said, evidence that the Prosecution relies upon. This Basara noted that he had been deceived and that snipers shooters were lining up. The witness had to see that and then let him say that he did not see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Bear that in mind, we'll consider how you conduct your cross-examination when you ask for further time or extension of -- further extension of time at the end of your cross-examination. Bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this page will be added.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, this meeting of 20 April was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Already in the evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Part of the evidence, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, in your statements, you focused on the census and you said that there were more Muslims and that there were a couple of thousand less Serbs. As a man who hails from a family that was not an Ustasha family, are you going to confirm or deny that in the Second World War at Susnjar, in a single go, in a single operation, 5.300 Serbs were killed by the Ustashas. Are you denying that or confirming that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Denying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is not true?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We always laugh at this Serb data of yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you trying to say that among those Yugoslavs there weren't any Serbs and that there wasn't a majority of Serbs in 1991 when Muslims and Croats were no longer in favour of Yugoslavia and the elections in which -- that Rasula won, don't they show that Sanski Most was majority Serb?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. Because in Sanski Most there were a great many citizens who were of Bosniak ethnicity, who worked in Austria, Germany, Slovenia and other countries and therefore they could not vote in the election and that's why the Serb side won.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you accept --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was rising just because of the compound nature of the question, if Mr. Karadzic can put single questions to the witness, it's preferable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Karabeg, that as for the overall number of neighbourhoods in Sanski Most, Serbs were an absolute majority in 45, a relative majority in 2, and that the population was mixed in 20, whereas the Muslims had 16 neighbourhoods with a majority of their own, then one mixed neighbourhood or actually eight mixed neighbourhoods?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said, Mr. Karabeg, that Serbs wanted to proclaim the entire municipality of Sanski Most a Serb municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's what they did on 3 April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Karabeg, that their proposal was to set up two municipalities, a Serb municipality and a Muslim municipality, out of the existing local communes of Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. I don't know whether they were thinking of creating two municipalities. They just wanted a division. They just wanted to have Sanski Most divided.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Divided into two municipalities, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not discussing two municipalities. Just a division. That is what the Serb side persistently asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So during the direct examination, you said that one side of a street was to belong to the Serbs and the other side to the Muslims. In Sarajevo, Zagreb, Belgrade, Mr. Karabeg, in all of these places where there are several municipalities, don't administrative boundaries run down streets or even within a single building? Administratively doesn't one part belong to one municipality and another one to another municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did not understand what I was saying, when I was explaining this. I said even one house. It wasn't like half/half. It wasn't Bosniak people on one side, Serb people on the other side. A street would be 200 metres long, Serb people, Serb. And then there is interruption and then Bosniaks live there, and then that is Muslim. That's as you put it. So this street of one kilometre or two is interrupted every 200 metres in that way, that it should be either Serb or Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you accept that Serbs were only counted -- counting on Serb concentrations and that Muslim concentrations should be a Muslim municipality, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I accept that, but that wasn't all of it. There was quite a bit of the Muslim parts that the Serbs wanted for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'm going to read a summary out to you. Muslim population concentrations. Tell me, was this supposed to be the Muslim or the Serb municipality? This is it: Sehovci, Trnova, Skucani Vakuf, Podbrezje, Okrec, Naprelje, Modra, Lukavica, Kijevo, Husinovci, Hrustovo, Gornji Kamengrad, Donji Kamengrad, Gorice, Dzevar, Denisevci, Mahala, Muhici, are all of these concentrations Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Serbs want to include in their own municipality any one of these concentrations?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wanted to include everything and they did include everything, ultimately, in their municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 04992? This is a statement of reasons for the establishment of the Serb Municipality of Sanski Most. In English, these local communes are already listed. Those that are part of the Serb municipality. So can we have this same page kept in English? Can we have page 2 in Serbian? Muslim -- actually the next one. This was just identification. Have a look at this now. It's in the Latin script, it's in Serbian so you can read it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to have this enlarged, please, if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sehovci, Trnova, Skucani Vakuf, it's simply not there, nor is Podbrezje, Okrec, Naprelje, Modra, Lukavica, Kijevo, Husinovci, Hrustovo, Gornji Kamengrad, Donji Kamengrad, Gorice, Dzevar, Denisevci, Mahala, Muhici, none of those local communes are there, those where there are large concentrations of Muslim population. So the Serb Municipality of Sanski Most consists of the following local communes. As you can see, all of those that were not included --

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have just had a polemic. You said that Caplje was a large Muslim concentration, Fajtovci as well, and on this list I see both Fajtovci and Caplje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are there Serb hamlets in Fajtovci and Caplje?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, we've just had a polemic. You mentioned that Caplje and Fajtovci had large Muslim populations and that is true and I see this here on this list that they would be part of the Muslim -- of the Serb municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there are Serb hamlets in that local commune?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which hamlets exist there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1679, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do note that part of this exhibit is already -- was exhibited yesterday as P3304, the decision of the Serbian people the Sanski Most municipality of 25 March. And also the 3 April --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What do you mean by part of this exhibit? Which is the more complete one?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The one that was exhibited yesterday I think has signatures on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And also the last part of it, the decision dated 3 April because this consists of two different documents. That was also exhibited as a document that was shown to Mr. Karabeg in his Brdjanin testimony and I'm just trying to find the exhibit number for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In conclusion, there is no need to admit it separately?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I don't think so, Your Honour. I mean, there are different versions of it. This is unsigned but it's the same documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If I get confirmation from Mr. Robinson or Mr. Karadzic, we can just do without admitting it. Let's proceed. Thank you, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, 3 April decision is P03325, so they are both in evidence already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, do you accept that the Serb side envisaged that there should be a Muslim municipality as well as a Serb municipality and that they should have both their respective Municipal Assemblies, police stations and so on? Is that what the Serb side envisaged and your side refused?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The result of that is that on 3 April 1992, the Serbs proclaimed the municipality of Sanski Most to be a Serb municipality and it was annexed to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Sanski Most already part of the community of municipalities of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not of Banja Luka. Of Bosanska Krajina. You know that there are two Krajinas, Ljuta Krajina, around Cazin, and Bosanska Krajina around Banja Luka and that's the one we belonged to before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have Rasula's diary? That is 65 ter 4988, or perhaps it has a joint P number but that's the number anyway, and then the Serb version, 154, and in English, it's page 139. Did you attend this meeting when General Talic and Colonel Basara came on 20 April and Major Zeljaja?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we zoom in on the left where it says in Cyrillic the meeting on 20 April, it says: "Present, Mirzet, Redzo, Sabic, Ante and Vlado." Vlado is probably Vlado Vrkes, a Serb?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you this is what Redzo says: [As read] "The official position of the Muslim people is to observe the peace. The SDA abided by the agreements and will of the Serb people." He reads the proclamation of the parties from 15 April 1992, agreement to carry out divisions in the municipality. Do you see that, Mr. Karabeg, that Redzo, in your presence, informed General Talic that agreement had been reached to carry out divisions in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, these are Rasula's thoughts. General Talic would not have come had all of that been well and fine. They would not have addressed him. He had deceived us too, because we thought the army, the JNA, that it was the people's army, but it immediately sided with you, which is only natural because more than 90 per cent of the officers were ethnic Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you see that he is actually referring to Redzo's words, he is not phrasing this himself? It says "Redzo:"

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can say whatever he wants.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: He can say whatever he wants.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, from yesterday's document, the meeting at the Islamic religious community, that it is said that time should be bought, there should be procrastination, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say the same to that document too. These are your thoughts. This is your way of thinking. I do not know whether that kind of meeting was ever held at the Islamic community.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, a minute ago you said he can say whatever he wants. Who did you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Rasula, the author of the diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not Redzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, not Redzo. The author of the diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So according to this diary, Redzo allegedly said that. So you are denying that, you are denying that Redzo said this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not true. That is not true. We tried not to be seen or heard at that meeting. We were so humble because the military representatives were in charge of the meeting. They were trying to represent themselves as some kind of peacemakers, who would ease all these tensions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Karabeg. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that meeting, Talic said, agree any which way you want but do it fast and do it in peace?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you this: This meeting was held and certain conclusions were reached. Within that framework we suggested to General Talic that he personally reads these conclusions on Radio Sanski Most through the media because then that would carry more weight, and the Serb people would accept that. However, it was stated that that was technically impossible. We said, "General, please, you have a telephone here. Do call Radio Sana, and ask them to carry live what you will say now." And he said, "No, I'm in a hurry." He said what you said just now: Do that and meet as soon as possible to get this done. We agreed on a meeting at 6 p.m., that is to say 1800 hours, not knowing anything. It was the municipality building. We had a meeting there, in front of the municipal building there was barbed wire, hedgehogs, two APCs. All of that was encircled. No meeting, no nothing. However, General Talic said to me, Karabeg, you as the representative of the authorities, if anything is wrong, please feel free to phone me, use this number. He gave me his telephone number. I think I called him on Wednesday. This meeting was on Monday and I just remember that when I did phone him and when I told the man at the telephone exchange who it was I was surprised that in about 20 seconds, I had General Talic on the line. I explained what the situation was, as you had put, nothing doing, the Serb side does not accept this, Rasula does not accept this, and he used a sort of swear word and said, "What is this? Why is Rasula not accepting this? I'll see about that with him." The next day was the holiday of Banja Luka. And I was watching the news and I saw a videoclip from that meeting where there was Karadzic, Mrs. Plavsic, General Talic and all the rest. They were all sitting there and I sort of said to myself, my goodness, why did he deceive me, why did he lie to me? And that's the way it was all the time after that. This is what they resorted to. This is how they deceived us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karabeg, I'm not going to check whether I was at Banja Luka at a particular point in time and why that would have been a bad thing for political personages to attend the celebrations of Banja Luka Day. But let's leave that aside. Are you saying that on 4 April, the Serbs declared that all of Sanski Most was the Serb municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was the 3rd or the 4th of April but it was the Serb Municipality of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have a look at this diary again, in English [as interpreted] 152 and in English, 138. Please look at this. Could this be zoomed in? The handwritten part, please. Please look at this, Mr. Karabeg. What it says here, on 16 April, the 2nd assembly of the -- the second session of the Assembly of the Serbian Municipality of Sanski Most. So you see that there was a Serbian part and you said that they claimed the entire one. Look at the agenda, please. The information on the results of the elections and inter-party agreement allocation of seats. So on 16 April they were still counting on the fact that there would be a Muslim municipality as well, is this what it says here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it says here. I can't see well. Let me tell you. There was the time when we discussed not about the divisions. First, they started with the police, they wanted people to sign a loyalty oath. There were Serbian police, they wanted everyone to carry Serbian insignia and they wanted a Serbian flag, with four Ss, to be flying over the police building and they wanted this to apply to everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, do you see here that under item 5 they speak about the transformation of the public security station? Do you wish to say that the Muslims and Croats who would remain to work in the Serbian police station were not supposed to swear loyalty to their employer and to promise that they would apply laws in their work?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, why should there be a Serbian police when we used to have the police of Bosnia-Herzegovina? It was lawful, it worked well, and it was broken apart by the Serb side who wanted some paramilitary or para-forces to be established and who wanted staff to declare loyalty and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we have the next page, please? You used to mention the SDK, the public audit service, and you used it as an example of something that Serbs had done wrong, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we see 140 in Serbian and, in English, 124? While we are waiting for that, Mr. Karabeg, did you understand that there was a political process underway in Bosnia and Herzegovina according to which the Serbs were to accept an independent Bosnia and Herzegovina and they wanted their conditions to be met, the conditions for them accepting an independent Bosnia-Herzegovina and you were all the while deceiving them through these false negotiations?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean false negotiations?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you saw in that document that it said that you should stall it and you should procrastinate in order to gain time.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this, please. A, B and C, look at C, please. Violation of all federal regulations, from the constitution to the laws, fiscal laws, the only regulations that are insisted upon are those according to which the federal state has obligations and not us. Then item 2. This is the session of the Executive Board, Mr. Karabeg, on 16 March. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you were a member of the Executive Board of your municipality and you were the president. Oh, no, I'm sorry, I apologise. This material was prepared for the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I can see the date. It says for the Executive Committee session and it's dated 3 March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see the Serb position, Mr. Karabeg, namely that the public audit service, the SDK, under the influence of the Muslim side is undermining, is destroying the federal state, undermining regulations, and, then under item 2, it speaks about the unlawful cessation of work of the public audit service and separatist behaviour in Sanski Most and so on? Do you see that the Serb side was making you aware of the fact that the SDK, the public audit service, was acting unlawfully, acting in violation of the federal and republican enactments and laws?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you something. The flow of funds was in the direction of Sarajevo, which is only natural, and what they were trying to do was to divert it, to divert the flow of funds and to make the SDK, the public audit service, work unlawfully. This was done pursuant to your wishes, to you, your desires and you wanted to replace this perfectly decent person in Sarajevo who was at the head of the DSK.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we see 1D?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the number? The interpreters didn't hear the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could this page and the previous one be admitted, please? No ruling was made regarding that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat the number you want to show us next?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D4245.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And with respect to the addition of additional pages from Rasula's diary, they are not included in your exhibit, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: My apologies. The 16th of April session wasn't and also this reference to this 3rd of March was not either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In light of the extensive use or reliance on this Rasula's -- Mr. Rasula's diary, is it not a good idea to admit it in its entirety or through bar table motion. Mr. Robinson because you objected to admission of this and Mr. Karadzic is heavily relying on it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct and I think our position is one of principle, to be consistent. Because we still believe that we should have the right to only those portions admitted which are discussed in court, but if the Chamber finds it more suitable to admit, as you've done with the Mladic diaries, the whole thing, then we understand that. But in principle we think that the rights of the accused are better protected when only those parts of materials from an unavailable witness are discussed with the witness in court and can be cross-examined.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Understood. I leave it to the parties. Those pages will be added. Yes, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would just add one thing if there is an emphasis on principle. This is something that Mr. Robinson and I have discussed and I believe agreed upon. The confrontation issue is not a matter of a bright-line principle but is a question of weight and I think this -- we maintain the position that there certainly are documents which are coherent and integral and should be admitted as such. This is a document which has been admitted in numerous previous cases under just that rationale and the issues addressed by Mr. Robinson, as we've discussed go to weight. So I think he wants to maintain his adherence to a basic underlying principle but I believe that he recognises that that gives way in certain circumstances to the practicalities of a particular document and the issue of how much weight is accorded to various portions, given the totality of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In any event, this is a good subject to be considered as a subject of a bar table motion in the future. Let's continue, Mr. Karadzic. Have you uploaded the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's been uploaded now. Could we zoom into the left column where it says, invitation to the non-Serb municipalities to join in. Yes, the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see this here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is there a translation available, Your Honour, in e-court? Because I don't have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has already been adopted with Mr. Treanor. I don't know what D number it was assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. This is a newspaper article, is it?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Apparently Mr. Reid informs me it's D286.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom -- rather scroll down, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: See, Mr. Karabeg, the Association of Municipalities of Banja Luka invited other municipalities. Please look at the end of this text. Signed by Ribar, in order for Bosnian Krajina finally to stop being poor and destitute. So on 4 May 1991, they send out an invitation to the Cazin Krajina and non-Serb municipalities to join them in order to experience just like they did an economic revival. We see the translation here. Whereas your position is that the Serbs wanted to -- wanted Sanski Most to annex to some other Serb municipalities and you wanted Sanski Most to join Cazin Krajina where the majority of residents were Muslim, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was an invitation, and anybody could send out an invitation. And we didn't want this. We didn't want to join Cazin Krajina. We wanted to join Bihac, and our wish was fully justified. Sanski Most had been destroyed, torched, people killed by those from Banja Luka, and it was liberated later on by those from Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, we are discussing 1991 and early 1992 here. There was nothing wrong at the time.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm simply making a comparison. It would be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we see 4988, please, the diary? English page 126. In Serbian, 142; in English, 126. In that meeting, attended by Adil, Mirzet, Ankica, most likely these are people from the SDK, and you say that you should all sit down to discuss how to take over the power?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Whenever we show the document, we just collapse the English page and zoom in the B/C/S page so that the witness can follow. The Chamber can follow the English pages on our personal computers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we see page 142 in Serbian, if we are going to show only the Serbian text. I'm not sure. 142, please. The right side, please, the right side. It says here --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, can Mr. Karadzic advise what meeting this is? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the witness will be in a better position to tell us this. This is the meeting of the SDK, the public audit service. They discussed the chief of the public security station and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where was this meeting held?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this one in which you participated, where Adil said that the judicial system should abide by the inter-party agreements and so on and you said that you needed to sit down and agree on how to take over power?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: With whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we scroll up, please? Three pages prior to this, we see that this was the 3 March. This was the preparation for the session of the Executive Board so there was a meeting on -- there was a session on 3 March 1992 where you discussed the unlawful work of the SDK and so on. These are your words.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, these ones here, do you see them?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it says here, Mirzet, the leadership in the electric utility company, talk to Bosko and so on then it says that the work of the public security station or rather the chief of the public security station is not good, and so on. Could we scroll down, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt again but I'm really not following in e-court which meeting Mr. Karadzic is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we go two pages before this, we will see that this is what was said on 3 March 1992 during the session of the Executive Board. Two pages back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think page 124 in English is the page which we saw earlier on today for the Executive Committee session, 3 March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I just saw something about November 1991 on the screen and that was what confused me. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, do you follow what this meeting is about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I would like to know. Perhaps I would remember who attended the meeting because you're now asking me about 1992 and it's 2011 now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So Mr. Karadzic, in order to put your question, just put your question one by one so that the witness can follow your questions. So you should have shown this first page and explained what this meeting is about and then you can come to his statement. But in any event, I note the time. It's time to take a break. We will have a break for half an hour and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Where were we? We were on Mr. Rasula's diary. Go back to page 126. And what was your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we get to page 126, you say there, inter alia, to sit down and reach an agreement on the takeover of power. What did you mean by that, unless you meant everyone taking over their own municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, page 126 for English and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. In English, it's 126. And it's 142 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, on the right-hand side; Mirzet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: See that here? You talked to Bosko and Bosko said to you that it was the fault of the parties?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Further down, further down. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: See, here you are, Mirzet, somebody wrote down what you had said and you said among other things, the second sentence, to sit down and reach agreement on the takeover of power. On 3 March, that's what you said, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. Especially now that you say Bosko, which Bosko? Bosko who?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Further down, you say the chief of the SJB is not good, should be changed. That's the public security station. That's at your request. Was he changed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not have anyone replaced or I could not make such requests. If a political party appointed someone, it was only that political party that could have replaced him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the SDS actually carry out what you had asked for, to replace Mr. Majkic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only laugh at that. I can only laugh at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was he replaced?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know because I was arrested on 25 May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: After that, was Vrucinic appointed who was not a member of any party and you confirmed that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's you who says that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that in your statements and I do not have time to call that up. You said that he was a person who did not belong to a political party?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to show it to you later. Can we have this page admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This will be added.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, in the beginning of April, did an explosion take place in a Serb yard and did that lead to mass gatherings of armed persons of Muslim and Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that. I just know that there was an explosion in a coffee bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A Serb coffee bar?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have 65 ter 05002?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P3324, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure that that's the number. A bit of patience, please. Here it is, that's the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at this. This is an assessment of the current security situation in the area of Sanski Most. The centre of the security services of Banja Luka, the state security sector and it says -- can you read this?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. Could it be enlarged a bit more, if possible? Right. Now it's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here that the situation had deteriorated and that it's characterised by, can we scroll down, ignoring the law, a chill in intra-national interethnic relations, tensions that lead to more organised self-protection of the population, a rise in crime and also aggravated conditions in the work of the organisations of the interior. Can we see the second page from the bottom now? A bit more, please. Thank you. This is it. You see this? The latest case of a mass gathering of armed population of Muslim ethnicity in Sanski Most and a pretext for that was planting an explosive against persons of Serb ethnicity and that led to requests for dividing the territory of the municipality. Can we go further down? It's 14 April. So that you can see the date. So it's 14 April. And the Serbs are not counting on Sanski Most being theirs. It is only the Serb municipality that they consider to be theirs. Can we have the heading, please? You see this, it's 14 April. Do you remember that, do you remember that gathering?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The author, please? I'd like to see the author of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Secret agents, or, rather, secret service agents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Top of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no, no, no. The lower part of the page where the author is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, this is operative 16600. It's on the top of the page. They used code names. They used codes. They do not sign their names. That's how they operate.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That doesn't mean anything to me but I told you until 6 April and after 6 April chaos reigned when the assembly was no longer working, when the Serbs obstructed everything with a view to proclaiming Sanski Most what they actually did on 3 April 1992, and they asked for the milicija, the police, to be the Serb police, that they wear Serb insignia and that they hoist a Serb flag on the police building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can this document be admitted? I beg your pardon, actually take a look at this. You said in your statement of the 24th and 25th of July 1991 [sic], that is page 7, 22130, 65 ter 22130. I'm going to read that out now in English. So that it is translated better than if I were translating it myself. It's not a quote. This is the essence: [In English] [As read] "Vrucinic had a map of Sanski Most and the Serbs had a proposal to -- of how to divide Sanski Most into two opstinas, Serb and non-Serb, a street by street, opstina-wise division. Vrucinic was the one with the proposal because he was not representing any party, and that this time he was still the head of the municipal planning department." [Interpretation] Later on, was he appointed chief of the joint police?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was he elected head of the Serb police?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that that did happen, because I was detained then. I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now look at 65 ter 04832. While we are waiting for that, the municipality of Srbac, was it called the Serb Municipality of Srbac?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I just know it as Srbac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why? Because there were no conditions there for having a Muslim municipality. Did you notice, Mr. Karabeg, that the prefix Srpska, Serb, is only assigned in places where there would be a separate Muslim and Croat ethnicity -- municipality and it never said Serb when it was just that kind of population and that municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, could you kindly repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that the municipality of Srbac is called Srbac. I don't know if it has any prefix or any other name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry for interrupting Mr. Karadzic but I see the LiveNote says Mr. Karadzic said that the witness's statement was 24th and 25th of July 1991. The statement is 1999 so I don't know whether it was a mistake with the court reporter or Mr. Karadzic actually said 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. He referred to 65 ter 22130 and then the list of documents says that it was taken in 1999. I think it's misspoken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If that's what I said, it was a slip of the tongue. It was either my slip of the tongue or the interpreter's.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, Crisis Staff of the Serb Municipality of Sanski Most, the Serb part, on 25 April 1992, certain conclusions are being defined and can we now have a look at conclusion number 7? Please take a look at this. I don't know if there is a translation for this yet. What was that? There should be a translation. Could the other participants please be given a translation. Look at what it says. Boro and Vlado are being entrusted with establishing contact with the representatives of the Muslim and Croat people, asking them to be loyal in the -- loyal in the existing organs of authority of the Serb Municipality of Sanski Most and that they should be told that they would be guaranteed all rights stemming from employment, civic rights and full equality of rights. You see the Serb municipality said that a number of Croats and Muslims would go on working in their government. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you. First of all I see this name: The Serb Municipality of Sanski Most. I do not see anything that says the part that is Serb. Let me say another thing. After that assembly meeting that was not held, I was frozen out. They didn't let me enter the building. I already spoke about that on the 17th and 18th of April, that we were in the municipality and left the municipality. I was given a decision as if I had been dismissed from my work because I did not report for work. However, the municipality building was blocked, there was barbed wire, hedgehogs, APCs. I have that decision. That is the way you did things. So you make sure that people cannot come to work and then they are dismissed from work because they had not come to work for seven days. And that is a document that states that and I happened to find that in my dossier, in my file at the municipality only after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the Muslim organs of government and the police station and the president of the municipality and everybody, didn't they just transfer to the left bank where they started setting up their own authorities?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me just take a look at this. Was it the fire department? No, what is there on the left bank? Some company whose building was used for that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that in that division, that they proposed to us and maybe you heard about it, that they proposed that we have the Sipa building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sipad?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sipa, not Sipad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sip?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Sip Sava where 90 per cent of the employees are Serb and they wanted to transfer us there so that we would create chaos, that we would have those people there. You know all the proposals of the Serb side were such that they were actually imposing problems upon us. They wanted us to have a chaotic situation in which we could not live or work properly and that turned out to be true indeed, after 25 May 1992 when we were arrested and when Sanski Most was shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And this Sip building, is that in the Muslim part of town?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, predominantly, no. The majority is that, yes, but you said it was the left bank of the Sana.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the left bank but, no, you cannot say predominantly, although indeed there are quite a few Serb neighbourhoods there and how. Dabar, Palanka, Lipnik [phoen], not to enumerate all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, could this document please be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, I'd like to hear from you in relation to the previous document 5002. It's security -- evaluation on security situation, as well as this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I was told that the 5002 was already admitted as Prosecution Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I was just looking at that one again, Your Honour, and thinking exactly the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that was exhibit, could you give the number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We will admit this Crisis Staff document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1679.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, is it true, or rather how many of you were arrested in late May in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, a large number were arrested, sent to prison building, to the Betonirka building, to the Vuk Karadzic school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know the number?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't, because on 25 May I was arrested myself so I couldn't learn of the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it 500?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So approximately 500?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so but don't quote me on this. This is what I heard from others.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how many of them were released? Do you know that 41 per cent were released after checks were made whereas 59 per cent were kept on and then sent to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I knew that four or five transports were sent to Manjaca, the largest one was on 7 July 1992. As for people being released, I was in prison when two elderly men, over 70, arrived. They brought us two pieces of bread. They said that they had been kept in the hall and then they were released and they were leaving and they gave us their two pieces of bread. One was called Rahmija and the other one was called Beco. It was in late June, early July. On the 28th of August 1992, I found myself at Manjaca and there I met the first one, Rahmija and I asked him what are you doing here? Weren't you released? He said you know what they gave us the papers as though they were releasing us but as soon as we left, somebody else arrested us and I was sent to Manjaca and Beco was sent elsewhere. So this is what they did. They falsely released people and then arrested them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we'll check that. Isn't it true that you said that the last large convoy of refugees from Sanski Most arrived in Travnik in 1995 and then you met them there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And isn't it true that in Sanski Most, before the war broke out, there were almost 30.000 Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that there were 28,300, according to the census from 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you explain, Mr. Karabeg, that out of 28.000 Muslims, only 400 to 500 extremists were arrested, justifiably or not? Those were the people who the Serbs considered to be extremists. And how do you explain that as late as 1995, there were still Muslims in Sanski Most leaving the place?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you how I explain it. Do you think that only those who were arrested in May were sent to Manjaca only during that period of time? You did that throughout the war, up until the 17th of September, all the way up until then. Do you know how many people remained in Sanski Most on 12 October 1995? 575 residents out of 28.300 residents and if you're going to mention these figures, well, don't focus only on one period of time. Look at the whole period of time, from May of 1992 until Sanski Most was liberated in October 1995. Look at what was done during the entire period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, in Sanski Most, in the town of Sanski Most, there could not have been 28.000 of non-Serbs. This figure applies to the entire municipality, not to the town itself, and then in 1995 you found 575 residents only, and that was after heavy fighting between Serb and Muslim forces; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Could we now see 65 ter 04906? Could we now see what this is about? These are the minutes of the 11th session of the Executive Board of Sanski Most Municipal Assembly held on 14 August 1992. Could we see page 4, please? Look at what it says here, Kalacun asked the president of the Executive Board to present the general view of the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina concerning the moving out of the Serb state. Rasula, Nedeljko, this is what he says: "We don't have a general position. We don't have instructions. Nobody is forced to move out. The basic attitude is that the citizens should decide where they want to live. If somebody wants to move out, they should be allowed to move out with certain supervision and protection. Those who wish to remain in the municipality will be allowed to stay only if they had not bloodied their hands or took part in any underhanded activities. Those who wish to move out will have to bear the costs of that themselves because we have no money for it." And then M. Lukic adds: "According to the international law, people cannot be prevented from moving out. Those who wish to leave should be allowed to do that and those who wish to stay should be allowed to do that too." This was not written up for the media, Mr. Karabeg. This is the session of the Executive Board held in August 1992. Do you see that this is why in March of 1995, you were still having convoys of people arriving and there was a difference between Muslims who had left and Muslims who had stayed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm telling you what I heard from others, 14 August 1992, I was already arrested at that time. I was arrested back on 25 May. I don't know what was happening in Sanski Most. I had no personal insight into that, what was happening from 1992 until 1995. However, I'm conveying the stories of people who were there, who knew. I told you about the torture, mistreatment. Had people had the relevant papers, all of them would have left because they were exposed to terrible abuse. However, they needed to obtain visas, they needed to have money for travel. It wasn't that hard reaching Travnik but then from Travnik one had to travel on to Croatia, to Slovenia and to other Western countries. I am telling you what others told me. I can't tell you anything about what happened in Sanski Most between May 1992 until 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that initially people had to sign consent on placing their property at the disposal of the municipality. Do you know of any case where some real property was transferred to somebody else, where the ownership was transferred to somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, those were few cases of abuse and foul dealing. You know what the procedure is, what procedure needs to be implemented in order for ownership to be transferred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in one of your testimonies, you confirmed that you were offered the opportunity to set up a Muslim municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Listen, we've been discussing it back and forth all day today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this offered to you or did you not accept it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nothing was offered to us. Only the Serbs were offered to have their own municipality, and these games were played until the 3rd of April 1992, when the assemblymen of SDS from the assembly, and some highly educated Serbs, got together and adopted an illegal decision proclaiming the Serbian Municipality of Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could this document be adopted, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1680, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see 22133, 65 ter 22133?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 17 April 1992, in a coffee bar of Toma Delic, was there a meeting that you attended there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there as a guest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now see page 1609? 6109, I apologise. 6109. On 27 May 1992 -- no, that's not the right document. We need 22133, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which is his 92 ter statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, the Brdjanin testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps that's included too. But, yes, this is the testimony from the Brdjanin case, if that's been admitted, then, yes, yes, that's the right document. It is. Now, let me read out to you what you said back in Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, 22133 is all of his previous testimony. 22133A is the Brdjanin testimony only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will read out to you what you said back at the meeting. You say: [In English] [As read] "On behalf of the SDS, there was Vrkes Vlado, Boro Savanovic and Tomo Delic and that was in his cafe. "Q. What was discussed at that meeting? "A. I think it was conducted in a tolerant atmosphere. In fact, Tomo Delic treated us to drinks, and he said that we should resolve the problem and that we would continue the talks, the most probable solution would be to split up the municipality building, that half would be given to us and half to the SDS." [Interpretation] On 17 April, Mr. Karabeg, the Serbs offered you half of the municipal building to set up your Muslim municipality, and now you're saying that the Serbs wanted the entire municipality for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. The Serbs took the entire police building. We went there and I think that further in my testimony you can see that, Tomo Delic portrayed himself as a great peacemaker. There were three or four kilos of lamb roasts there, several bottles of wine, et cetera, and we had talks there, and Tomo told us there, "Leave the municipal building. We cannot suppress and control our extremists who want to attack you." And there were police workers there. And later on, we found out that Tomo Delic was the leader of those extremists, the Serb Defence forces, the SOS. And when meeting us, he was begging us to agree to this because they couldn't control their extremists. I remember that meeting very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true what you stated back in Brdjanin?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, is it true, did I understand you well, you wanted half of the building but you didn't want the municipality to be split, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you. We were housed in the municipal building because the people had been chased out from the police building because they refused to carry Serb insignia and they didn't want to sign the loyalty oath.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that you had the Green Berets and that you, your police commander, was at the same time the commander of the Green Berets and that this is why you refused to divide the police force because the Serbs did not have their Green Berets and whereas you did? Did you have Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some in Vrhpolje and Hrustovo. What have you got against those Green Berets?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, we have nothing against two Green Berets unless they have two tonnes of explosive material.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
