utterances.text: That's what you're claiming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let me show you the document. 1D00011. While we are waiting, do you know that we banned and expelled the Serb armed forces, the SOS?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the first I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at this. This is the municipal court of Sanski Most in 1997, that is to say after the -- after Sanski Most was taken over by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is the decision declaring Enver Burnic dead. And please look at the bottom of the highlighted portion. It says here that both proposed witnesses, in their statements, stated that Enver Burnic was very patriotic, and he expressed his patriotism when, as a commander of police in Sanski Most, he refused to accept the legality and legitimacy imposed by the authorities of the Serb aggressor and actively worked on preparing armed resistance to the Serb aggressor, and he wore on his uniform the insignia of the Patriotic League, the lilies. Did you know Enver Burnic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he take part or, rather, is what it says here, what the Judge says here Ahmet Tatarevic, is what he says here true because it was signed by the judge, Ahmet Tatarevic. Do you know the judge?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is what it says here true, about this man Enver?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to tell you the truth, I doubt it very much because usually things are exaggerated with the statement of reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to tender this document into evidence now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How is this relevant, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it's relevant in relation to the subject of the police and the division of the police and why they didn't accept the transformation of the police force into two stations, because they had their goals and objectives, and their chief of police worked to prepare an armed struggle. And he changed the insignia, not the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just a moment, Your Honour, if I may have a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can take a look at the last page in Serbian, the signed and certified page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think the witness has confirmed anything in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And it's very difficult on the part of the Chamber to find the relevance of this decision. We will not admit this, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can't tell you now once you've made your decision but I'd like to say that this is court evidence, that the joint commander of the police station, Enver, worked --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You will have another opportunity to tender this. You do not have much time with this witness. I think it's almost about five minutes left and I don't know how much more time you will be asking for but plan your cross-examination to be focused. Or it will be too late.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I had hoped to have the whole day today or at least this session. Because you see we are presenting documents which call into question the testimony of this witness. I can't overrule his statements through any other witness but through him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Plan your cross-examination to be able -- so that your cross could be concluded by the end of this session, which is 12.30. We'll see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we now have 65 ter 05125, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Take a look at this document, please, it's dated 5 August 1992. The security services centre of Banja Luka and it links this up to the material of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Serbia, it's strictly confidential, and it says -- well, can you read it? You can read it yourself. It says, in the Sanski Most area, in the last two months in Sanski Most municipality, there has been a great deal of activity by certain paramilitary groups that have broken free from the army command, and which are waging their private actions which are reflected in the fact that they are putting explosives, planting explosives, setting fire to houses, killing, looting, and another -- committing other crimes against the Muslim and Croatian population in order to gain -- for material gain and to persuade them to leave. That's the first paragraph. And I'm just going to read the last sentence of the second paragraph which reads, "The SOS, we registered four such groups including the so-called SOS, the former paramilitary formations of 30 men strong, which was formally put under the command of the war unit here as a sabotage platoon but nobody has full control over it." Can you see that, Mr. Karabeg? Can you see that Tomo was right when he said forces were in existence which were outside their control and this was in August, the problem existed as far as August?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't understand me. Tomo Delic was at the head of the SOS. And he duped us. He was at its head. And now you're presenting all this material that this document was written, and all the rest of it. It's 5 August. So from 25 May to 5 August, they could have done many things, and did do them, but you're denying this whole period. You say that none of that happened. And this whole conversation boils down to the fact that the Serbs, that the Serb side, did not do any of these things and that it was all under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, the Serb authorities are pointing this out two months from 5 August backwards two months to the end of May, for two full months they were running amok and they asked that they be disbanded.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say it wasn't just the 25th of May, from the 25th of May. It started in April, the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this can be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1681.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 05077 next, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Take a look at this, Mr. Karabeg. On 30 May, which means a lot before the other affair, the Serb forces of Sanski Most make a proclamation and complain that they are being treated or they are complaining of their treatment and that they want to go elsewhere. Because they are not welcome in Sanski Most and haven't been welcome by the authorities. And because of the very complex security situation and counter-propaganda, and applying the provisions of the formation of the SOS of Sanski Most, "We hereby proclaim... " and then it goes on to say -- may we zoom down the page, please -- I hope that the other participants can follow the translation. "Because individuals and the authorities are expanding their propaganda to belittle our contribution, we have decided to leave this territory and to fight for the ideals of Serbian, Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and to protect the Serbian people, to struggle for this outside Sanski Most and we shall be informing -- and that the area command will inform you of this." So that was at the end of May, Mr. Karabeg. They were forced to leave Sanski Most. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, don't ask me again. I said I know nothing about that. I know nothing about the situation after the 20th of May, 1992. So please don't, refrain from asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you said that nobody touched them, whereas they were interfered with.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I tender this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On what basis do you think we should admit this, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Directly contradictory to what the witness claimed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm telling you: Don't ask me. I know nothing about that. I know nothing about the situation after the 25th of May 1992. You're showing me a document that was written after my arrest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Karabeg is saying he doesn't know but how is this document contradicting his statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But he said a moment ago that until 5 August they worked unimpeded whereas here it shows that that was not true. This document shows that that's just not correct, that even before that they were pushed into a corner, that the authorities pushed them into a corner and that they became one of those uncontrolled elements that the authorities were criticising.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you said yourself the 5th of August. You mentioned 5 August yourself. And then you said all this yourself, the 30th or whatever the date was. You're speaking about these matters yourself. I'm telling you that I know nothing about these matters. They are your documents, the ones you're presenting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, Mr. Karadzic was addressing the Chamber. Can you had help us, Ms. Sutherland, in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, as you've noted, the witness -- it doesn't -- this document doesn't contradict anything the witness has said because he said he can't speak to the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, is this document dated at all?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 30 May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, we will not admit this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have to wait for another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Karabeg, do you know that the Serb side tolerated the existence of the Muslim armed forces and the Green Berets themselves in town, and considerable forces in Hrustovo, Vrhpolje and Kamengrad, right up until they launched offensive operations against the Serbs, the Serb civilians and the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I only knew about the forces in Hrustovo and Vrhpolje because the population organised themselves over there in those two places and they were members of the Territorial Defence to begin with and when the Serb forces attacked them, and surrounded them, and took about 30 -- they took about 30 Serb officers prisoner and forced the people to go up for an exchange in Serbian Krajina, so those Serb officers were returned. But the people managed to gain their freedom.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that to help those captured Serbs, the people from Hrustovo, Vrhpolje, Kamengrad, were allowed to pass on to free territory in Bihac, as it was called?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only the other two places, not Kamengrad, Hrustovo and had Vrhpolje and that was their aim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May we have 1D00030 next, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, is there any problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is something technical about wind. I already once suffered a terrible pain in my back because of the cold wind. And it's going to repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As did one of my colleagues already. Yes, I hope that can be sorted out very soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we now look at page 40? 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the highlighted portion. It's a book that you're well aware of, and you were in the editing board. Do you see there who the key people were in Bosnia-Herzegovina in the formation of the Patriotic League and Green Berets? The names are Sefer Halilovic; Sulejman Vranj, Sule; Munib Bisic; Brko -- is Atif Saronjic from Sanski Most, for example?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then there is Mustafa Hajrulahovic; Rifat Bilajac; Zico Suljevic; Meho Karisik; et cetera. May we go on to the next page. Anyway have you heard of these people and did you know that they were members of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard of these people, they were all in the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, take a look at Sanski Most. Just before the highlighted portion, it says: [As read] "The situation in Sanski Most, when it comes to preparations for the defence of the municipality, and including the municipality and defence preparations during 1991 and beginning of 1992, was not satisfactory. As far as I know, the Patriotic League in Sanski Most did not exist."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Are we on correct page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we are. But I don't know about the English, the English page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the page number of this? 40. Does it start with "Parallel to the increasingly more prominent presence"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's next paragraph. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, look at this highlighted portion. It says parallel with the increased presence, et cetera. It says that the Green Berets, a group like that, was active in the town proper, and in another document, it says, in the Mahala or centre of town and Muhici. You saw that yesterday, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you okayed -- authorised this book and Vrhpolje, Trnovo, Hrustovo and part of Kamengrad are all mentioned but you see that it existed in the town itself. You were one of the editors of this book so that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: May we look at the next page, please? Mr. Karabeg, can you see -- the -- first we can look at the part up here, where there is a reference to blockaded roads, I don't have to read out all of it. You can look at it yourself. What happened in April. And then the presence of locals who were armed. Ifet Hukanovic led them, procured weapons. I see Madam Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt again but just back on that question, the compound question that Mr. Karadzic asked

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "So you okayed, you authorised this book and Vrhpolje, Trnovo, Hrustovo, part of Kamengrad are all mentioned but you see this existed in the town itself ...," and then the second, the third question, you're one of the editors of the book and then we get the answer, yes. Perhaps if Mr. Karadzic can clarify which -- what the witness was answering yes to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I thought the witness answered yes to all of his question but Mr. Karabeg, could you confirm, do you remember the question and answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just confirm that I'm one of the editors of that book. He asked me whether I was one of the editors. He asked that at the beginning and the end of his question. And I said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you approved of the book as truthful and correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not me. It was the entire team.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this encircled part where it says -- look at this part, 300 locals who were armed in Vrhpolje, is that what it says here, intensive preparations beginning of April, roads were blocked around the village, also armed guards were placed there and also specially designed -- designated patrols were supposed to monitor enemy activity and follow the entire area. Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is what is written there. You had all of Sanski Most under your control. I was never denying that Vrhpolje and Hrustovo, and I said people had self-organised themselves there and that they were putting up resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it says there that Muslims did that and it's saying Vrhpolje?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not denying that. In Vrhpolje and Hrustovo there are no Serbs, it's Muslims who were there. I did not challenge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see the bottom of that page and then the next page? You see here that on 15 April, there was a review. Can we have the next page, please?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, read it until the end. What was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence of Vrhpolje.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Next page. The top of the next page, please. Have a look at this: 300 armed soldiers, the late Arif Hukanovic commanded them, Beco Buljubasic, former JNA captain, and so on. And look further down. The first clash took place between the 14th and 15th of May. Actually, the forces of Vrhpolje deployed around the school put up an unexpectedly strong resistance to the aggressor and the enemy was forced to withdraw. So on the 14th and 15th of May, there were clashes already because a Serb unit was defeated there. Can we have the next page? Please focus on this where it says, actually, Avdic's and Hukanovic's assessment was that offensive combat operations should start and losses in personnel and materiel should be inflicted upon the enemy. And then it says, where the platoon from Sanica advanced and the other platoon, and so on and so forth. So Mr. Karabeg, this is not the Territorial Defence. These are manoeuvring units that are launching offensives against Serb neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's what this book says.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have just said that it was the Territorial Defence and now you're denying it. You are quoting from the book and you say that it's the Territorial Defence, 300 armed men, and now you are denying it. The Territorial Defence is legal. It's a legal formation of the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the Territorial Defence authorised to attack Serb neighbourhoods?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you attacked all of Sanski Most. You had it all cut up and you held all of it ultimately and you will already declared it the Serb Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can this be admitted, this part of the book?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be added to the MFIed exhibit D1677.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 5445.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Serb Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Autonomous Region of Krajina, Crisis Staff Banja Luka, on 11 May. To the presidents of all the municipalities, so it is in the plural, to the presidents of municipalities. And these are the conclusions, namely that the deadline for handing over illegally procured weapons has been extended until the 14th of May 1992 at 2400 hours. Paragraph 2: [As read] "The deadline that expired today was extended at the request of citizens of all ethnic backgrounds and as was explained by a desire to have weapons returned in a peaceful way and without police interventions." Do you remember that this was proclaimed, that weapons should be returned?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but unfortunately that pertained only to the Serb people -- actually Bosniaks and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can this be admitted? Actually, what is written here does it not say that persons of all ethnic backgrounds are asking for an extension of the deadline?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what is written is one thing but what was actually carried out was a different thing altogether. You write it up and you implement it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1682, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 05118.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at this, public security station of Sanski Most is informing the Security Services Centre of Banja Luka and it says, "Pursuant to your letter we hereby provide information on which weapons have been handed over until now." Some weapons were seized, some were handed over. If necessary, we can have this enlarged for you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you say anything, Mr. Karabeg?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He asked me whether this should be enlarged and I said that it should be enlarged and now I can see it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: LP 283. Lkar 23. Automatic rifles, for instance, 230. Semi-automatic rifles, 155. Then hand grenades, 2. And look at explosives, 3.000 kilograms, three tonnes of explosives were handed over. And let us look further down, it says during the search, another 140 kilograms of explosive were found that had not been surrendered until then voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the lower part of the table. Did you see in those minutes what Sabic was saying, who was in charge of procuring explosives, and that's what the book also says that some explosives were obtained. Who got these explosives and for what purposes?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, you are showing me a document that I'm not aware of because I was under arrest. Now you are saying to me that on the basis of that order, decision, what was proclaimed was some voluntary surrender of weapons, what the CSB Banja Luka did. I am telling you that this only had to do with the non-Serb population. You are denying that. You are saying that that pertained to the entire population. Now, I don't know what you want me to tell you on the basis of all of this. I don't know about any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the last page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the point of showing another page, having heard the witness, what he's going to say about this document? It's simply a waste of time, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The signature is that of a person who did not belong to any political party, and that is what the witness himself said, and this person was Mr. Vrucinic who was appointed as the chief of the public security station. He is a professional and he is providing information on what was surrendered and what was seized. This is a summary. This is what the police came to learn. And I wanted him to see the signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I answer? I was on very good terms with this Vrucinic and I held him in high regard. I was arrested, I was taken to prison and then transferred to Betonirka and then from Betonirka, I was returned to prison again. There was this young man whose name was Tonci, who was a Serb guard, and one morning he called me at 5.00, he told me to stand up and to spread my arms and legs, and he started beating me. He beat me from 5 until 7 o'clock. I left, and then when he came to work again, when his shift came again, after two days, he called me in yet again at the same time, he beat me with a truncheon and I left. And next time he called me in again and again he started beating me and he beat me -- let me just finish, please, let me finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karabeg, I'm sorry to interrupt you but do you have anything to add about this Mr. Vrucinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. No, he does belong to a political party. He was DP. He would not have been appointed chief of the Serb police, the then milicija, if he was not a man who belonged to a political party. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the SDP, not the SDS, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean SDP? What are you on about? What did you have there except for the SDS? Who accepted, yes, and those who did not accept, hand grenades were thrown.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A moment ago, you said SDP?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, you said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted this document on the surrender of weapons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see any basis to admit this document through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were arrested on the 25th of May. On the 26th you were interrogated for the first time?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 25th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said in your statement dated the 24-and-5 July 1999, on page 9, 22930, you said that some Papric said to Kurbegovic, you see, Redzo, where this led to, where this -- what is this, this forecast, where this forecast led your people and then you said, all right, we are in prison but why don't you let Meho Kaplic go? He's retarded. And then you say later he was released. In one statement you say after one hour. And during the direct examination, you said after one day. Is this correct, what you said here?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I do not remember exactly. I just know that he was released. Papric walked in with a beret, a Green Beret, SOS as you would put it, yes, Meho was released, yes, I just don't know when. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Can we briefly look at 65 ter 18922? Do you know that in the Serb Municipality of Sanski Most, there was civilian protection that dealt with civilians?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, because from the 25th of May 1992, I was under arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Radio Sana in Sanski Most said the civilians from Mahala and Muhici should go to the stadium until they deal with the extremists?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: You say that I'm an extremist and I was under arrest and I did not have an opportunity of listening to that radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us see what the civilian protection says here for this period from 15 July until 15 October 1992. After war operations in the territory of town, the staff took part in evacuating the population that was not involved in resistance, transferring them to other parts of town. So it's not only within the same municipality but within the same town, from a neighbourhood where there was fighting, the population is being evacuated into a different part of town. Do you remember that that is obligatory on the basis of the Law on National Defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, do mention at least one citizen of Serb ethnicity who was killed in town, whereas I will tell you about tens of non-Serb citizens who were killed in Sanski Most. Except for Vrhpolje. Now, you tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And who was the first casualty in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Can we scroll up and see what else the civilian protection was doing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see the point of putting this document, in particular, this was not translated. I would like you to move on to your next topic. Your time is limited, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we see 1D00015, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is the list of the soldiers killed in Jasenovac. Could we see the next page, please, these were the soldiers of the 6th Brigade who were killed upon arriving in Sanski Most. Could we see the next page, please? Dobrijevic, Predrag in Trnovo. Cedo Lazic near Hrustovo. Goran Rajlic in Podvidaca. He was wounded by a Muslim extremist who ambushed him. Vaso Stupar in Bosanski Milanovac, Mirko Cicic in Caplje. Rade Malic in Hrustovo. Are all of these Serbs killed by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you claim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it says so in the document.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's your document. That's your blabbering.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then to go on, one page after other, Hrustovo, Tramosnja, all of these people were killed there, just this document lists 17, 18, who were killed from ambush in Kruvari and so on. So you do not take into account this, this document was not drafted for propaganda reasons, this is a record?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, tell me who, where and who killed them?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you hear of Tramosnja? You mentioned that these people were killed in Tramosnja, Gornja Tramosnja and Donja Tramosnja. There was not a living soul there, no Croats, no Muslims, who lived there. There were no people living there. Some who did commit some murders ended up in prison. And you just are adding up various pieces of information here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So there was some Serbs in prison, right? Do you mean Betonirka or at the police station?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: In prison. Prison is a prison. And Betonirka was a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, do you know that Adil Draganovic upon coming to Sanski Most found at least 30 investigations pending against the Serbs who had armed -- harmed some Muslims and that to this day, people are prosecuted pursuant to those criminal reports and investigations?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. It is possible but I don't know about that. And about them being put on trial, I don't know about that. Although it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In Betonirka they held investigations, they interviewed people, some of you, and then some were released and some were returned to prison, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Betonirka was vacated on 7 June and 550 residents of Sanski Most municipality were transported, whereas the seven of us from Betonirka were sent back to prison where we remained until 28 August when we were transported to Manjaca as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that Vujanovic -- who was in charge of the prison, would come to protect the prisoners, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are all kinds of stories circulating about Vujanovic. I personally --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He was the warden and then there were guards coming in and out. Did you say that people came there to take revenge because they had been given a bad grade at school or they had some unsettled personal accounts?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had one such case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where it was personal?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where they came to beat me. And one man protected me and got me out. His name was Savic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who are those people who came to beat you, were those some old unsettled accounts?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing of the sort. I didn't know those people. They wore olive-drab uniforms. I was in garage number 3. They called my name, came out, there were three men standing in front of me. One of them said, balija, just look at you, look at the sight of you, go wash your face. And then there was some water source, 30 to 50 metres away. I went there, I turned the faucet, there was no water coming out. And the man who had shouted at me just look at your sight, he came to me and he said, you know what he said? He said Mirzo, I'm sorry, forgive me, I had to mistreat you. I had no other choice. I need to provoke you because the other two came with me to beat you. I will try to get you out of this. This is how that story ended. I went back to the prison building and nobody touched me, so there were some decent people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in your statement, on 24th and 25th of July 1999, 65 ter 22130, page 12, you said that Vujanovic was still the commander of the prison, that he visited you and others, he didn't beat anyone, and he would come to protect the prisoners, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I have nothing bad to say about Drago Vujanovic, I personally have nothing. Now as to other things that may have happened I know nothing about that. But when it comes to me he treated me fairly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you said it in this statement.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, it's possible. I don't want to smear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it possible that you were suspected of being given a list by Osman Brka of the Serbs to be liquidated and of the list of Serb young men who were to be circumcised and girls to be raped?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no such list. This was published in the media in Sanski Most, that I was in charge for raping Serb children, no, for circumcising the boys up to the age of three, for raping girls ages 6 to 10 and this was the propaganda aired on Radio Sana, they said that they found lists on me. And you know what people are like. Nobody wondered whether that was normal, whether anybody could come up with such an idea. Everybody said how stupid can you be and have those lists on you. That was the propaganda at the time. Even the Bosniaks said that when I was arrested. They said, look at how stupid he is. He actually had those lists on him. That was the power of that propaganda.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have a bit more time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How much do you have in mind, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we have quite a lot of documents which would be relevant for this witness. I don't know how much time, perhaps 20 odd minutes in the next session. We will prioritise the documents during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will take a break, Mr. Karadzic, after which you will have 15 minutes to conclude. We will resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are only sitting until 13.45 today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We need to break half an hour so shall we resume at five past 1.00? Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, what you've just described, this brawl, the beating that you described, was the man's name Veselinovic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veselinovic did some beating too but I didn't mention that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that you let Veselinovic go from the firm, you sacked him, and that he used the occasion to get his revenge on you and beat you up?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't dismiss him. I didn't sack him. He dismissed himself. If you want me to explain, I can. He didn't turn up for work, he was a bad worker, and I was the head of the service, the commission expelled him, he felt this, he asked me whether he could get an agreement releasing him from his duties because he wanted to go to Italy, and then when I was in Betonirka he made me clean the toilet, he made me kneel and he went over me at that point, well, he behaved normally but I thought he was going to beat me but the worst thing was this expectation, my waiting with him looming above me for 15 or 20 minutes and then 15 minutes later he swore at my -- called me a balija, he said, you see, I'm giving you a job to do, whereas you didn't want to give me my job. He was a guard in Betonirka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And he started beating you, is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And my whole head was bloody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And he told you he let you know that that's because he was sacked and you spoke about that in your 1995 statement, on page 6 and 7, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you mentioned a professor being beaten because he gave somebody a bad mark, a teacher being beaten up, something like that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's throw some more light on a particular matter. There are quite a lot of differences in your statement. I haven't got time to go over all differences and discrepancy, however the last meeting you had with your friends was in hodza's house, right, on 25 May -- April?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which friends? Which friend or friends?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me just check if it was April or May. It was 25 May, Redzo Kurbegovic, Nihad Kljucanin, and Rifat Bahtic, Haso Osmanovic and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible. But it wasn't in hodza's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the Islamic community, their building or what?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, up until that time, had many people, both Serbs and Muslims, left the town, left Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, yes. Especially the young people, the youth, whom they wanted to forcefully mobilise into the JNA, so to avoid going to the battle front in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you, Hasib Kamber, and Bahtic, and that is on page 39, Ziklija Bahtic you said that they should be more active because their families were out of town. You gave them radios and told them to report on the situation in town; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that statement of 13 September 1995, page 39, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't give those assignments to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At that meeting, not perhaps you personally, but Rifet Bahtic and Hasib Kamber were they there and were their families out of town?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether their families had left town but they were at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this same statement of September, 22128, page 3 you say that the imam's house, hodza's house in Sanski Most, you say that Fajko Biscevic -- Faik Biscevic or whoever noticed that daily meetings would be too obvious and that you had decided to meet the following morning at 11.00, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why too obvious, Mr. Karabeg? Why couldn't you meet normally, publicly?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we worked underground, illegally. We weren't allowed to breathe, to move around. Do you think it was a free territory like it is here? You know best how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says there that these two were given radios and that they were told to report back about the situation in town.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never said that but it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you were arrested in the meantime so there was no next meeting, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, your arrest, do you link that up with these secret meetings and the distribution of the radio stations and everything else? Do you link the two?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you they weren't secret meetings as far as we were concerned, they weren't. But they mistreated us, they persecuted us, they followed us, followed our every step. They had masses of people to do that. Some were honest, some were dishonest, some were thieves. But anyway, we were followed, monitored.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There are quite a few inconsistencies and I would like to remind you of one. Is it true and correct that you said that Basara arrived with the intention of keeping the peace and protecting the non-Serbs from the extremists?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We even put his name forward. We wanted to make him honorary citizen of Sanski Most. But we didn't know what role he was actually playing. It was common knowledge what Basara turned out to be throughout that period. So he was playing a double role, a two-faced game, and as I say, we even proposed put him forward for honorary citizen because we thought he was doing a good job to begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then you said that he attended the Municipal Assembly sessions?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't attend.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you said that in your statement of 1999, on page 3, on the 24th and 25th of July 1999, to be exact, page 93 -- page 3. But then in 2002, you reneged and said you weren't certain whether he attended.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I'm saying. Basara could not have attended because Basara arrived at the end of March 2002 [sic] as the commander of the 6th Brigade. He came from the Pakrac theatre of war, and when I said that we even proposed him, we wanted to proclaim him honorary citizen of Sanski Most, well, you know it was only the Municipal Assembly which could reach such a decision, and so if that was the case he would have been at the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So is it true that you did not have direct insight into the functioning of the Crisis Staff? Did you mean the Muslim Crisis Staff or the Serb Crisis Staff or both?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know which statement of mine you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you did have an insight into the work of the Muslim Crisis Staff, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't the Crisis Staff. The Muslims did not have a Crisis Staff. We had a body at the level of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the name of that body?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was similar to the term Crisis Staff. I can't quite remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you agree that the Army of Republika Srpska took a decision on 12 May at the assembly meeting and -- that the army came into existence as of 20 May when the JNA withdrew?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood your question. What was the date you mentioned? What's that first date?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The first date is 12 May where the assembly took the decision to form an Army of Republika Srpska. Up until the 19th of May it was the JNA and the Army of Republika Srpska came into existence as of 20 May, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which assembly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Serbian Assembly in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm a little unclear about this because in your 1999 statement on page 8 you said that Talic [phoen] told you that he would inform Karadzic of the conduct of the Serbs in Sanski Most, Rasula and others. Now, that was from the 22nd of April. Now, do you accept that on 22 April, the Army of Republika Srpska did not exist and Talic could not, nor did he want to report to me about anything because I wasn't in charge of that army?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Karadzic, interpreters did not hear the witness's answer. What was your answer? Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you say that Talic told you that he would inform Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I said, that he swore when he mentioned Rasula and that he would inform him and that he would deal with the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But he didn't say that he would inform Karadzic, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell me, please -- you're looking at me so that is a warning for me to wind up, I think. Now, do you accept that in the Sana valley, that it was aflame on 23 May with an attack at the check-point in Hambarine and that in the Sana river valley there was an elite unit of the Muslim Patriotic League at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sana valley is a broad concept. You can ask me just about Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, did you hear that the conflicts in neighbouring Prijedor -- how far is Prijedor, 50 kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: 28 to 30 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Right. 30 kilometres. Do you know that the conflicts began there on 23 May with the killing of Serb soldiers, Serb reservist soldiers at a check-point?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just heard what you did in Prijedor. And how much you did, and how many people you killed and how many you expelled, but I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that Mirza Mujadzic writes in an article that he cannot understand how, at the end of May 1992, in the Sana valley, the elite unit of the Patriotic League was routed so quickly and then you say, and now you say that Sanski Most, the forces in Sanski Most, 900 armed men, were not part of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I am Mirzet Mirza Karabeg. So don't ask me about Mirza Mujadzic. Ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, is it true that part of these people who were arrested, Kurbegovic and others, that they were released very quickly afterwards?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where? Kurbegovic was arrested together with me and transported to Manjaca and from Manjaca he went to Bijeljina and spent another year and a half there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But in your statement, you said that these men were released soon, quickly afterwards. Now, who was released? Who else was released from your cell? You were in cell number 2, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In prison, in prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, could Mr. Karadzic just give me a transcript page for the reference to the statement, please, sorry a page number for the statement he's referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will, straight away, with pleasure. Just bear with me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While I'm looking for that, who interrogated you, Mima or Stanic and what was their profession?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was interrogated by several people but at the beginning it was Stanic, Rajkica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, time to conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was he a professional investigator?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A reserve?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a judge in Sanski Most. Unfortunately, he roams around freely and he is a lawyer in Prijedor today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to answer Madam Sutherland, it is the statement to the Bosnian authorities given in 1995 and page 7. You say: [As read] "Fajko Biscevic; Kurbegovic, Redzo; Sabic, Suad; Talic, Bego and another man whom I don't know -- whose name I don't know, these people were released three days later and Emir Seferovic, Said Sinanbegovic, Hasanbegovic and others were in my cell?"

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only Bego Talic who was released. All the rest of them were with me right up until the end and some of them spent more than a year or a year and a half in Batkovici, the camp there. I was released from Manjaca and on 31 October 1992, I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So Bego Talic was a Muslim too but he was released, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Bego cannot be a non-Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, and my last question: Is it correct that at the police station, at the station, Macura beat someone or rather he was a policeman before the war, came to the station, and beat Kljucic saying, what have you done to make these two communities not be able to live together?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Nihad and me. He came to beat us, he came into our cell in the prison and beat us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And he accused you of bringing about a situation whereby the two communities could not live together any more?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what he said but I know what he said about me at the pre-election meetings. I told the people, come out to vote, and whole families should come out to vote. Grandfathers, grandchildren, and so on. And he took that to be the disruption of brotherhood and unity and he beat me and he beat me very badly. I don't know about Nihad, I know that he threatened Nihad with something too but I can't say. But let me add you always had some excuse to beat someone. If somebody were looking from outside, they would say, well, these people are quite right to beat them because you always found some excuse. You blame me for disrupting brotherhood and unity, for inciting the people, young and old, to go and vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, I don't think that anybody must be allowed to be beaten but in your statement of July 1999, on page 12, you said that Macura beat people and said that you should be blamed for the hostile relationship between the two ethnic communities who could no longer live together side by side, that you said that.

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said -- I did not, no but he blamed me for disrupting brotherhood and unity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that the two communities could no longer liver together?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here is the statement:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. It's -- you said a minute ago that was your last question. And then continue. It's difficult to find the significance of these lines of questions. Your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please put your last question and you can submit later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was my last question. I just wanted to tell you that I cannot disclose what will be stated in the final arguments because Ms. Sutherland is going to use that and act accordingly and I know exactly what I'm aiming at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Do you have any re-examination, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Karabeg, I'd like you to look at one document. On page -- today's transcript, page 22 and at pages 43 and 44. There were questions put to you by Mr. Karadzic in relation to the police force and swearing of the loyalty oath. This is on page 22. If I could have 65 ter number 004818, please. If we could go to -- Mr. Karabeg, we can see there that this is a -- you have mentioned earlier in your testimony that -- during cross-examination at one point, that it all started on 11 April 1992, when the police were asked to sign the loyalty oath and put the insignia. This is a document from the CSB in Banja Luka dated 10 April and if I could just draw your attention to paragraph 3 on page 3 of the English, and I think it's on page 3 going over to page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We collapse English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 says: [As read] "Upon the receipt of the new post assignments, authorised employees will have to sign a solemn declaration, the text of which is identical to that of the solemn declaration from the previous Law on the Internal Affairs and the employees were given the deadline of 15 April 1992 to sign the declaration. Those who fail to sign the declaration by that date will have their employment with the SRBiH Ministry of Internal Affairs terminated." And then paragraph 4: "Police employees shall wear ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: "Police employees shall wear new uniforms and sleeve insignia with the word 'milicija' written in the Cyrillic script and blue berets with the tri-coloured flag (red, blue and white) badge." Is this consistent with what you were trying to explain earlier in your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: MIRZET KARABEG [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I tender that document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3330, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just one other matter, Your Honour, earlier today at transcript pages 49 to 51, there was a document discussed in relation to the SOS, if you recall, and Mr. Karadzic sought to admit it, and Your Honours asked for my assistance in relation to whether it contradicted the witness's evidence and I said to you that it hadn't because the document was dated 30 May 1992. And he couldn't -- said he couldn't talk about it and then Your Honours conferred and decided that you didn't want to admit the document. In fact, when I read the transcript back in the break, it's not inconsistent with this witness's evidence because the witness does speak about the SOS committing acts prior to 30 May 1992, so in that regard, I would have no objection to the tendering of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We admitted a document which refers to SOS group, which was 65 ter 5125 and was admitted as Exhibit D1681. What we didn't admit was an announcement regarding -- by Serbian Defence Forces on 30 May.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that was 65 ter 05077.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. So the Chamber found that two cases to be different. But now you --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I think the proposition that Mr. Karadzic was putting to the witness was that this is a document dated 30 May and see, it shows that these forces were being impeded in doing what they wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you but you're moving now to -- for those -- that document to be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection to the document being admitted simply because in the document it does refer to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But we already ruled on it. Unless you move to tender that, we will not revisit the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can we move for reconsideration?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There will be another opportunity to -- for the Chamber to admit that document. Not this time. We leave it at that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour, and just a couple of other matters. Yesterday, we said that we would get back to the Chamber in relation to MFI D1678 which was discussed at transcript page 18741, it was a document that had -- I stated that the MFI said it was a partial translation or a summary translation. In fact it is a full translation done by AID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: So the MFI status can be taken off that document if Your Honours are minded to do that. [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That was our observation. That will be admitted in full. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Another document yesterday, the book, the large book which was MFIed, D1677, and certain pages that Mr. Karadzic has put to Mr. Karabeg have been admitted. I just wanted to make sure that we are reserving our right to tender other parts of the book once the book has been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And finally --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're done with your re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So we can excuse the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, I just have one other document which was put by the Defence to Mr. Karabeg and I wanted to know whether it was being admitted in its totality and that was 0 -- 1D00015, which is also 65 ter number 05097.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it was admitted previously as D6. You mean the list of killed soldiers in Sanski Most?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If my recollection is correct that was admitted when our first witness came, Ahmet Zulic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour and I led that witness and I overlooked that matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it concludes your evidence, Mr. Karabeg. On behalf of our Chamber and the Tribunal as a whole, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you, too, for working so properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Gaynor and I need to switch places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure it's practicable to continue but could you let us know who the next witness is?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The next witness, Mr. President, is KDZ-379.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Shall we go into private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now back in open session. Unless there are any other matters to raise, to be raised, we will adjourn for today and resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There is Lukic and Lukic case, yes. We will resume at 1.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 15th day of September, 2011, at 1.30 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
